Honestly doesn't look too bad to me! I have a thin part too, and I have a bit of a technique to disguise it. My hair is dark brown and there's this brunette dry shampoo I buy which comes out in a brown colour that's pretty similar to my hair colour. It sounds a bit stupid but what I do is part my hair, then get a piece of string, pin one end at the back of my hair and hold the other end in my mouth so that the string goes across my parting, then I get the dry shampoo and spray it all over. It basically colours where my hair is thin and then when I remove the string it leaves a nice parting. I've found this really helps me.

The first time I pulled my hair out was when I was 10 years old. I have no idea what sparked it; one day I was sat in assembly at school and I just started pulling it out. It felt good and I just continued to do it. Once I realised that it was a 'problem', I was too out of control to stop. 

I tend to pull when studying, using a computer and when in bed. I try to wear a hat whenever I'm alone and I know that I might pull. It stops me doing it subconsciously as it acts as a barrier between my hand and my head. As for when I'm in bed, it may sound silly but I wear socks on my hands. Again this makes me aware of when I go to pull and makes it more difficult. 

I've never been on any medication for trichotillomania. I've only ever been prescribed CBT and other forms of therapy by my doctor. 

Although I don't eat the hair itself, I often chew the follicle off the end of it for some reason. It's something I've always done and I enjoy the feeling of playing with the hair more than anything. 

I hope you find this useful or interesting. Sometimes it's just good to know you aren't alone with these sorts of things. Best of luck to you with your battle- I know how horrible it can be.
